title: 0.1 second check
ig_caption:
Send this to whoever pays for ads and ignores a tenth of a second.

Website speed and conversion rate, from a Deloitte and 55 study for Google: 37 European and American brand sites, over 30 million user sessions, late 2019. Every page in the user journey got 0.1 seconds faster on four mobile speed metrics. Retail conversion rates rose 8.4% and retail shoppers spent 9.2% more.

Don't read it as a promise. The data's from late 2019, and the gain only showed up when every page improved on all four metrics. Your site may behave differently.

If you're paying for clicks, check your landing page speed. Paste your ad page into Google PageSpeed Insights and read the mobile tab. It takes a minute.

Source: Deloitte and Google, Milliseconds Make Millions (web.dev case study).

If you pay for traffic, a tenth of a second is a budget line.

A Deloitte and 55 study for Google tracked 37 European and American brand sites and over 30 million user sessions in late 2019. When every page in the user journey got 0.1 seconds faster across four mobile speed metrics, retail conversion rates rose 8.4% and retail shoppers spent 9.2% more.

Two caveats. The data's from 2019, and the gain needed every page to improve on all four metrics. Your results won't match it exactly.

Before your next ad budget goes out, paste your landing page into Google PageSpeed Insights and read the mobile tab. We'd start there.
